key_insight: OmniVerifier-C1 replaces simple True/False judging with a graded verifier that breaks complex multimodal rules into smaller parts and scores them individually. This gives a more nuanced, informative critique of generated visuals in rule-governed settings.
problem_solved: Traditional visual verifiers often struggle with complex prompts or environmental rules because they output only binary decisions and cannot explain partial compliance. This paper addresses the need for finer-grained evaluation in compositional multimodal tasks.
method: Automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components.
Assigns pointwise scores to each component instead of producing only a binary verdict.
Aggregates these graded judgments into a continuous, more informative verifier signal.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this enables more robust evaluation of generative visual models in complex scenarios where partial correctness matters. It can improve debugging, benchmarking, and training feedback for multimodal systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing prompt/rule decomposition into sub-requirements and scored outputs
Side-by-side comparison of binary verifier vs graded verifier
Radar or bar chart displaying component-wise scores across multiple rule criteria
Icon set illustrating compositional rules, scoring, and feedback loops
paper_title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
paper_authors: Bowei Liu, Xinchen Zhang, Xuhuan Li, Tianlin Zhang, Kaian Jiang
